key_insight: A cycle-consistent neural surrogate can predict tokamak edge plasma fields quickly while also recovering the underlying control inputs and estimating prediction uncertainty.
engineering_relevance: This enables near real-time edge-plasma analysis for parameter scans, optimization, control, and digital-twin workflows where full SOLPS-ITER simulations are too slow.
method: Conditional U-Net maps five control parameters to 2D SOLPS-ITER plasma-state fields.
A frozen forward model is paired with an optimization-based inverse method to enforce cycle consistency.
An ensemble MLP predicts midplane and divertor profiles with uncertainty estimates to flag missing-data regions.
evidence_signal: The forward model reports normalized RMSE below 2.6% and Pearson correlations above 0.95, while cycle-consistency raises average cyclical R² from 0.59 to 0.99 and recovers all five control parameters with Pearson r≥0.97.
watch_item: Performance may depend on database coverage and warm starts, since cold-start inverse runs had about 30% outright failures.
paper_title: Cycle-Consistent and Uncertainty-Aware Neural Surrogates for Tokamak Edge Plasmas
